paper.title: Near Optimal Adversarial Attacks on Stochastic Bandits and Defenses with Smoothed Responses

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial attack (strong adversary) on stochastic bandits: attack cost against UCB / Thompson sampling
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Guarantees are for the attacker (cumulative attack cost to force a fixed learner algorithm to pull a target arm T-o(T) times), not for the learner.
unmapped: Objective is the adversary's cumulative attack cost to make a known learner algorithm (UCB / Thompson sampling) pull a target arm T-o(T) times
Strong adversary observes chosen arm and realized reward before corrupting
settings.definition_quote: In the study of attack strategies, the goal of the adversary is to manipulate the learner into pulling some target arm $T-o(T)$ times, while minimizing cumulative attack cost, defined as $\sum_{t=1}^T |\alpha_t|$.

settings.name_in_paper: Lower bounds on attack cost, two Gaussian arms (lower bound)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Lower bounds on the attacker's cost against fixed learner algorithms (UCB, TS, eps-greedy); guarantee concerns the attacker.
unmapped: Objective is the adversary's attack cost needed to force the learner onto the target (suboptimal) arm
settings.definition_quote: In this section, the bandit environment consists of two arms giving Gaussian rewards $\cN(\mu_1, \sigma^2), \cN(\mu_2, \sigma^2)$. The mean $\mu_1 > \mu_2$ and the 2nd arm is the target arm.

settings.name_in_paper: Defenses with smoothed responses against a strong adversary (competitive ratio)
unmapped: Strong adversary: corruption chosen after observing learner's action and realized reward
settings.definition_quote: This section will prove bounds on the collected rewards of the form \REW \ge (1 - \eps)\OPT - o(T), where $\REW$ is the total reward collected, as measured by the true empirical means, and $\OPT$ is the expected reward of the optimal policy ... In this section, pre-attack rewards and post-attack rewards are assumed to be bounded in $[0,1]$.

symbols.Delta_a_plus: max(0, mu_a - mu_K), where K is the adversary's target arm

conditions: learner runs UCB (Algorithm 2) with index mu_hat + 3 sigma sqrt(log t / N_a)

source.label: thm:UCBAttack
source.quote: With probability $1- \delta$, for any $T$, using the proposed attack strategy ensures any non-target arm is pulled $O(\log \log T)$ times and total attack cost is $\widehat{O}(K\sigma\sqrt{\log T} + \sum_{a\in [K]}\Delta_a^+)$.

results.notes: Quantity is cumulative attack cost. Also guarantees each non-target arm pulled O(log log T) times. Hat-O hides log log T factors; mapped to O_tilde.

symbols.Delta_a_plus: max(0, mu_a - mu_K), where K is the adversary's target arm

conditions: learner runs Gaussian Thompson sampling (Algorithm 4) with posterior N(mu_hat, 1/N_a)

source.label: thm:TSAttack
source.quote: With probability $1 - 2\delta$, for any $T$, using the proposed attack strategy ensures any non-target arm is pulled $O(\log\log T)$ times and the total attack cost is $\hatO(K\sqrt{\log T} + \sum_{a\neq [K]} \Delta_a^+ + K (\sigma+1)\sqrt{\log\frac{\pi^2 K}{3\delta} })$.

results.notes: Holds with probability 1-2delta. Sum index printed as a ≠ [K], interpreted as non-target arms.

bound.regime: T > B, B a sufficiently large constant

conditions: K = 2 Gaussian arms N(mu_1, sigma^2), N(mu_2, sigma^2), target arm 2 suboptimal
otherwise learner pulls optimal arm more than T/26 times with probability 0.9

source.label: thm:UCBLowerBound
source.quote: Assume the learner is using the UCB algorithm as in~\cref{algo:ucb}. For any $T > B$, if the adversary spend an attack cost less than $\Delta + 0.22\sigma\sqrt{\log {T} - 1}$, then with probability 0.9, the learner pulls the first arm more than $T / 26$ times.

results.notes: Lower bound on attack cost any adversary must spend against UCB.

bound.regime: T > B, B a sufficiently large constant

conditions: otherwise learner pulls optimal arm more than T/10 times with probability 0.81

source.label: thm:TSLowerBound
source.quote: Assume the learner is using the Thompson Sampling algorithm as in~\cref{algo:TS}. For any $T > B$, if the adversary spent an attack cost no more than $\Delta + 0.1\sqrt{\log T}$, then with probability 0.81, the learner pulls the 1st arm more than $T / 10$ times.

results.notes: Lower bound on attack cost against Thompson sampling.

bound.regime: T > B, B a sufficiently large constant

conditions: learner uses eps-greedy with exploration rate 2c/t
otherwise learner pulls optimal arm more than T/4 times with probability 0.8
tuning: c is the eps-greedy exploration constant

source.label: thm:eps-greedyLowerBound
source.quote: Assume the learner is using the $\varepsilon$-greedy algorithm with a learning rate $2c/t$ for some fixed constant $c$. For any $T > B$, if the adversary spent an attack cost no more than $c\cdot \Delta \log T / 6$, then with probability $0.8$, the learner pulls the 1st arm more than $T/ 4$ times.

results.notes: Lower bound on attack cost against eps-greedy.

source.label: thm:smoothMyopic
source.quote: Fix any $\eps > 0$, for a sufficiently large $T$, with probability $1- 1/T$, \cref{alg:smoothMyopic} achieves the following: \[ \REW \ge (1 - \eps)\OPT - o(T). \]

results.notes: Lower bound on collected reward REW = sum mu_{a_t}: REW >= (1-eps) T mu_star - o(T), w.p. 1-1/T. The -o(T) term is omitted from the expression. Competitive ratio 1-eps.

bound.regime: T sufficiently large; additive o(T) loss

source.label: thm:smoothMyopic
source.quote: Fix any $\eps > 0$, for a sufficiently large $T$, with probability $1- 1/T$, \cref{alg:smoothMyopic} achieves the following: \[ \REW \ge (1 - \eps)\OPT - o(T). \]

results.notes: Duplicate view of Theorem 6 as the competitive ratio value; the paper calls it achieving (1-eps) competitive ratio.

source.label: thm:quantal
source.quote: Fix any constant $\eps>0$, for a sufficiently large $T$, with probability $1-1/T$, \cref{alg:quantalRResponse} achieves: \[ \REW \ge (1 - \eps)\OPT - o(T). \]

results.notes: -o(T) additive term omitted from expression. Inconsistent lambda choice between algorithm and proof.

conditions: attack strategy with sublinear budget exists

source.quote: Fix any algorithm $\ALG$. There exists some constant $\eps > 0$ and an attack strategy with a sublinear budget such that the learner achieves no better than $1- \eps$ competitive ratio, specifically, \[ \lim \inf_{T\rightarrow \infty} ({\REW(T)} / {\OPT(T)}) \le 1 - \eps. \]

results.notes: Impossibility of competitive ratio 1; eps depends on algorithm. Derived from Fact 1 (He et al. 2022).

cited_results.setting_description: Attack cost to force UCB learner to pull target arm, two Gaussian arms with gap mu and noise sigma
